name: Melanotan II + Semax stack

lead: Melanotan II is a synthetic melanocortin peptide that darkens skin and can suppress appetite, so people use it for sunless tanning and a leaner look. Semax is a Russian heptapeptide derived from an ACTH fragment, used in Russia clinically and elsewhere as a nootropic. People who combine them seek tan plus cognitive or mood effects, and the two share a link to melanocortin receptors.

Human research on Melanotan II is mostly early phase studies from the 1990s and 2000s on pigmentation and erection; no study has examined the combination. Semax data are mostly Russian clinical work and animal studies.

paras: Both are discussed as peptides administered by injection or nasal routes; users in forums talk about combining them as a stack. This entry does not describe amounts or preparation.

Reported Melanotan II harms include flushing, nausea, mole and freckle darkening, priapism and case reports of kidney injury; health agencies in several countries warned against unlicensed tanning jabs from 2007 onward. Products sold online are unregulated and quality concerns are documented. Semax is not approved in most countries.

chain: Darker, more even tan with less UV exposure (Semax added for focus and mood)
angle.text: Melanotan II drives melanogenesis through MC1, darkening skin. Semax is added for its reported cognitive and mood effects rather than for appearance.

lead: The Melanotan II and Semax stack is a combination of two peptides taken together by some looksmaxxing and biohacking users. Melanotan II (MT2) is a synthetic analogue of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone used to tan skin; Semax is a heptapeptide analogue of an ACTH fragment used in Russia and promoted elsewhere as a nootropic. [1][2]

Users pursue the stack for appearance and function: MT2 for a tan achieved with less UV exposure and, in some accounts, reduced appetite; Semax for concentration and mood. A looksmax.org poster plans MT2 to make tanning more efficient and keep collagen intact with less UV, and another asks whether it could darken brows, beard and hair. [3][4] Melanocortin pathways are a common thread, as Semax has been reported to interact with MC4 and MC5 receptors, though its mechanism is not established. [2]

No clinical trial has tested the combination. Melanotan II was studied in small early human studies of pigmentation and erection and has been the subject of case reports and regulatory warnings. [1][5][6][7]
infobox: Unlicensed as products in most countries; Semax Rx in Russia [2][1]

paras: Melanotan II was synthesised by University of Arizona scientists seeking sunless tanning agents in the 1980s. It is a non-selective melanocortin agonist that drives tanning via MC1 and is thought to affect sexual function via MC4. It can darken moles and freckles and cause erections. [1]

Semax's name comes from the Russian for 'seven amino acids'. It was described in 1991, is a prescription drug in Russia (on its List of Vital and Essential Drugs since 2011) with listed uses including stroke and cognitive disorders, and is sold online as a nootropic elsewhere. Most findings come from animal work, including raised BDNF in rodents. [2]

Forum discussions focus mainly on Melanotan II. Posters discuss pairing it with tanning-bed sessions or tretinoin, asking if it darkens red hair, and homemade nasal sprays from vials. [3][4][8] Semax is mentioned as a companion nootropic. This entry does not reproduce any preparation or amounts.

Melanotan II side effects include flushing, nausea, vomiting and appetite loss. Reports describe priapism and a case of renal infarction possibly linked to it. [1][5][9] The UK MHRA stated in 2008 that the tan jab is an unlicensed medicine that may not be safe, and agencies in Norway, Denmark and Ireland issued warnings between 2007 and 2009. [1] A 2026 review describes dangers of injectable peptides and other unregulated biohacking drugs. [10]
Whether Melanotan II raises melanoma risk is unclear; a 2013 review found no conclusive evidence, and a 2021 review suggested higher risk among users may reflect more UV exposure. [1]

No studies found on the combination. For Melanotan II alone, a 1996 pilot phase I study in three male volunteers and later small trials of erectile function examined its effects. [6][7][11][12] An animal study in 2024 reported antidepressant-like and antistress effects of both Semax and Melanotan II in stressed rats. [13]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, Melanotan II threads concern tan efficiency, effects on red hair and freckles, and DIY delivery; Semax appears as an add-on. [3][4][8]
